variables.definition: Probability of rejecting the null under the same specified alternative
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Beta and power refer to the same test, sample design and specified alternative distribution.
Beta is a base-one probability between zero and one.
limitations: Power typically varies with the alternative effect size and assumptions; a single unconditional power value can be misleading.
A failure to reject does not prove that the null hypothesis is true.

models.title: Earnings-per-share forecast error, predicted minus actual
models.summary: The owner defines earnings forecast error as predicted minus actual.

relationship.original_equation: Forecast error = forecast earnings per share − actual earnings per share
relationship.translation_notes: All values are currency per share; the sample profile is USD per share.

variables.definition: Analyst forecast of earnings per share for the specified entity and reporting period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Comparable realized earnings per share for the same entity and reporting period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Forecast EPS minus actual EPS under the stated sign convention
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Forecast and actual use the same entity, earnings definition, currency, period, share basis and split adjustments.
The signed convention is forecast minus actual, matching the owner example.
limitations: Some forecasting literature uses actual minus forecast, reversing the sign.
The cited research uses this difference as a numerator and then scales it by prior share price; this record returns the unscaled difference.
A single forecast error is not a measure of repeated-sample estimator bias or forecast precision.
